nodes.name: Co-Cr Spinel Coprecipitation and Calcination
nodes.procedure: CoCr₂O₄ and Co₂CrO₄ nanoparticles were prepared using a one-step alkali-driven coprecipitation approach (in 1 M KOH electrolyte), followed by calcination. The bulk nanoparticle films on glassy carbon were prepared by drop casting and dried overnight.

nodes.description: OER performance in O₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH with LSV/CV cycling and chronopotentiometry
nodes.source_text: To compare the electrocatalytic activity of CoCr₂O₄ and Co₂CrO₄, we performed linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) and cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements using a rotating disk electrode (RDE) in O₂-saturated 1.0 M purified KOH... A 90% Ohmic drop (iR) correction was applied... CoCr₂O₄ exhibited slightly better OER activity... overpotential of CoCr₂O₄ after the first cycle is ∼370 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²... continuous decrease in its overpotential to 343±2 mV (at 10 mA cm⁻²) after 100 cycles... can maintain the low potential for ∼100 h

nodes.description: OER performance in O₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH with LSV/CV cycling and chronopotentiometry
nodes.source_text: overpotential of CoCr₂O₄ after the first cycle is ∼370 mV at 10 mA cm⁻², lower than that of Co₂CrO₄ (395±2 mV)... no activation was observed for Co₂CrO₄... the activity of Co₂CrO₄ is maintained during the first 500 cycles... after 1000 cycles, the overpotential of Co₂CrO₄ increases to 445±2 mV... maintains the potential for only ∼60 h... The compensation resistances are 10.5±0.1 Ω for CoCr₂O₄ and 27.9±0.2 Ω for Co₂CrO₄

nodes.characterization_summary: Both CoCr₂O₄ and Co₂CrO₄ exhibit cubic spinel structure Fd-3m with lattice constants of 8.309±0.002 Å and 8.232±0.002 Å respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both CoCr₂O₄ and Co₂CrO₄ exhibit a cubic spinel structure Fd-3m, as revealed by the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) data shown in Fig. S1a, b.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanoparticle sizes are 17.3±4.6 nm for CoCr₂O₄ and 18.5±5.5 nm for Co₂CrO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the sizes of the CoCr₂O₄ and Co₂CrO₄ nanoparticles are 17.3±4.6 nm and 18.5±5.5 nm, respectively (Fig. S1c, d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co and Cr are uniformly distributed across nanoparticles with Co/Cr ratios of 0.6±0.1 for CoCr₂O₄ and 2.3±0.1 for Co₂CrO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM/energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) images shown in Fig. S1e, f reveal that Co and Cr are uniformly distributed across the nanoparticles with Co/Cr ratios of 0.6±0.1 and 2.3±0.1...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge shows Co oxidation state in CoCr₂O₄ changes from ~2.0 (pristine/100 cycles) to ~3.4 after 1000 cycles with shift to higher energy by ~3 eV and decreased pre-edge intensity indicating increased octahedral coordination. Co₂CrO₄ changes from ~2.0 to ~2.4. Cr K-edge unchanged for both.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after 1000 CV cycles (yellow curve), it shifts significantly toward higher energy values (by ~3 eV)... The Co oxidation state of CoCr₂O₄ was estimated to change from ~2.0 in the pristine state and after 100 cycles to ~3.4 after 1000 cycles... the Co oxidation state of Co₂CrO₄ increases from ~2.0... to ~2.4 after 100 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p₃/₂ peak fitting shows dominant CoOOH on CoCr₂O₄ surface after 1000 cycles. O 1s shows O1 (529.5-530.0 eV, lattice oxygen) and O2 (~531.0 eV, defective/hydroxyl) with increased O2/O1 ratio after cycling. Cr 2p₃/₂ broadens in CoCr₂O₄ due to dissolution; sharpens in Co₂CrO₄ after 1000 cycles matching Cr(III) octahedral.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Our peak fitting analysis of the Co 2p₃/₂ spectra reveals that CoOOH is dominantly present on the CoCr₂O₄ surface after 1000 cycles... O1 at approximately 529.5-530.0 eV, corresponding to lattice oxygen... O2 at ~531.0 eV... Cr 2p₃/₂ spectra of CoCr₂O₄ after 1000 cycles, resulting in indistinct peaks...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman on 100-cycle samples shows spinel modes A₁g(~687 cm⁻¹), E_g, 3F₂g. CoCr₂O₄ A₁g intensity decreases rapidly >1.40 V vs RHE with blue-shift 688→690 cm⁻¹ indicating Cr dissolution and lattice contraction. Co₂CrO₄ A₁g stable. Broad ~550 cm⁻¹ peak indicates Cr(OH)₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: both samples contain five Raman modes of A₁g, E_g, and three F₂g... intensity of the A₁g band (at ~687 cm⁻¹ of 100-cycle CoCr₂O₄ decreases rapidly at above 1.40 V vs. RHE... A₁g band of CoCr₂O₄ is slightly blue-shifted from 688 cm⁻¹ to 690 cm⁻¹... broad Raman peak centred at... ~550 cm⁻¹... match with... Cr(OH)₃ reference material.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine CoCr₂O₄ retains spinel structure at surface. Pristine Co₂CrO₄ shows ~2 nm rock-salt CoO surface phase. After cycling, both show amorphous surface layers 1-2 nm thick.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high resolution aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) was employed... the surface of pristine CoCr₂O₄ retains the spinel structure... surface of Co₂CrO₄ spinel nanoparticles is covered by a rock-salt structure CoO phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: APT reveals uniform Co/Cr distribution in pristine CoCr₂O₄ (0.56±0.02). After 100 cycles: surface Cr/O depletion, K/OD enrichment 2-4 nm depth. After 1000 cycles: further Cr depletion (Co/Cr=0.98±0.04 surface).
nodes.evidence_snippet: cross-sectional atom map in Fig. 6a shows a uniform distribution of both Co and Cr in the pristine CoCr₂O₄ nanoparticle... The reconstructed 2-4 nm surface regions... are depleted of Cr and O...

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA increases for CoCr₂O₄ from 13.5±0.1 cm² to 52.0±0.1 cm² and for Co₂CrO₄ from 13.5±0.1 cm² to 32.5±0.1 cm² after first 100 cycles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Our ECSA measurements... confirm a considerable increase in ECSAs for both CoCr₂O₄ (from 13.5±0.1 cm² to 52.0±0.1 cm²) and Co₂CrO₄ (from 13.5±0.1 cm² to 32.5±0.1 cm²... during the rapid Cr leaching of the first 100 cycles.
